trial_court: Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track,1st Court, Raiganj, Uttar Dinajpur in Sessions Case No. 56/2002(in Sessions Trial No. 12/2003)
case_name: Samir Kumar Pal vs The State Of West Bengal
facts_of_case: Deceased Jhuma Pal was married to the appellant according to Hindu Rites and Customs on 4th December, 1997. She was subjected to physical assault by the appellant in an inebriated state. After some days, the appellant and her mother sent her to her parental place by assaulting her on demands of dowry.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
legal_principles.held: The prosecution examined as many as 17 witnesses and exhibited a number of documents. The defence however did not examine any witness of its own.

legal_principles.principle: The prosecution case must be free from contradictions and embellishments.
legal_principles.held: The evidence of the prosecution witnesses suffered from embelishments and contradictions.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is directed against the judgement and order dated 21/22nd January, 2004 passed by Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track,1st Court, Raiganj, Uttar Dinajpur in Sessions Case No. 56/2002(in Sessions Trial No. 12/2003) convicting the appellant for commission of offence punishable under section 498A and section 306 of the Indian Penal Code.
